extracted.intended_audience: Institutions and members of the public submitting filings, comments, protests, waiver requests, or motions to intervene in federal agency proceedings (e.g., Department of Education Campus-Based programs, DOE export proceedings, FERC dockets)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for preparing and submitting filings (applications, signatures, proof of mailing), public comments, protests, and motions to intervene in Federal Register notices and agency dockets; includes deadlines, acceptable submission methods, required content, and evidentiary standards for contesting preliminary determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of Mailing of Paper Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit paper documents when permitted by mail, we accept as proof one of the following: (1) A legible mail receipt with the date of mailing stamped by the U.S. Postal Service; (2) A legibly dated U.S. Postal Service postmark; (3) A dated shipping label, invoice, or receipt from a commercial courier (FedEx, UPS, etc.); (4) Any other proof of mailing acceptable to the Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department does not accept (1) a private metered postmark or (2) a mail receipt that is not dated by the U.S. Postal Service. Note: the U.S. Postal Service does not uniformly provide a dated postmark; check with your local post office before relying on that method. All institutions are encouraged to use certified or at least first-class mail. Hand-delivery of paper documents is not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Submission Deadline Time Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The deadline for electronic submissions is 11:59:00 p.m. (Eastern Time) on the applicable deadline date. Transmissions must be completed and accepted by 11:59:00 p.m. to meet the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to electronic portals specified (e.g., COD, eFiling). The Secretary may consider on a case-by-case basis the effect that a major disaster or other unusual circumstance has on an institution's ability to meet deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: FISAP and Signature Page Original Signature Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The FISAP signature page must be signed by the institution’s chief executive officer with an original signature and mailed to the designated FISAP Administrator address (P.O. Box 1130, Fairfax, VA 22038). For overnight delivery, mail to the provided street address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FISAP itself and other specified documents must be submitted electronically through the Common Origination and Disbursement website (https://cod.ed.gov). Supporting application documents should be scanned and emailed to the designated contact (e.g., alanna.nelson@ed.gov) where instructed. Signature pages for other applications (Work Colleges Program) have the same original-signature and mailing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: DD Form 2065 and DD Form 1375 Completion and Supporting Documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: DD Form 2065 records the sponsor’s disposition instructions for remains and associated costs; a signed copy accompanies remains to the port mortuary and will be uploaded into DCIPS. DD Form 1375 is used to request payment of interment allowance and must be signed by the claimant and include all documents (e.g., receipts for services performed or paid for).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both forms are presented to the sponsor by the Casualty Assistance Officer (CAO) who aids in completion; the CAO returns completed forms to the Service Casualty Office (SCO) which uploads them into DCIPS. The Privacy Act Statement on the forms notifies respondents of appropriate disclosures. Sponsors (typically family members) must submit payment or claims per the described process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for a Qualifying Conduit Hydropower Facility
rubrics_metrics.description: To be a qualifying conduit hydropower facility under FPA section 30, the facility must meet statutory criteria including: (a) the conduit used is a tunnel, canal, pipeline, aqueduct, flume, ditch, or similar manmade water conveyance operated for distribution of water for agricultural, municipal, or industrial consumption and not primarily for generation of electricity; (b) the facility is constructed, operated, or maintained for generation of electric power and uses for such generation only the hydroelectric potential of a non-federally owned conduit; (c) the facility has an installed capacity that does not exceed 40 megawatts; and (d) on or before August 9, 2013, the facility is not licensed, or exempted from the licensing requirements of Part I of the FPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission staff assess whether operation will alter the primary purpose of the conduit. Preliminary determinations may be issued; parties may file comments contesting whether the facility meets qualifying criteria and must set forth their evidentiary basis when contesting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and Formatting Requirements for FERC Filings
rubrics_metrics.description: All filings must: (1) bear in all capital letters the appropriate filing type header (e.g., 'COMMENTS', 'COMMENTS CONTESTING QUALIFICATION FOR A CONDUIT HYDROPOWER FACILITY', or 'MOTION TO INTERVENE'); (2) state in the heading the name of the applicant and the project number of the application to which the filing responds; (3) state the name, address, and telephone number of the person filing; and (4) otherwise comply with the requirements of sections 385.2001 through 385.2005 of the Commission’s regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments contesting staff’s preliminary determination that the facility meets qualifying criteria must set forth their evidentiary basis. Filings must also comply with service and proof-of-service requirements (18 CFR 385.2010).

rubrics_metrics.name: E-Filing, eComment, and Character-Limit Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission strongly encourages electronic filing via the eFiling system. Commenters can submit brief comments up to 6,000 characters, without prior registration, using the eComment system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eComment submissions must include the commenter’s name and contact information at the end of the comments. For assistance with eFiling/eComment, contact FERC Online Support or use TTY numbers provided. Paper copies may be mailed to specified addresses if not filing electronically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to Intervene: Timeliness and Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any motions to intervene must be received on or before the specified deadline date for the particular proceeding. There is no fee or cost for filing comments or intervening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A protest may also serve as a motion to intervene so long as the protestor states it also seeks to be an intervenor. Follow the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure (e.g., 18 CFR 385.210 and 385.214) and file before the listed deadline. The Commission’s Office of Public Participation (OPP) can help members of the public with filings and navigation of the processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Review Timing under NGA/Commission Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to section 157.9, within 90 days of notice the Commission staff will either: complete its environmental review and place it into the Commission’s public record for the proceeding; or issue a Notice of Schedule for Environmental Review indicating milestones and the anticipated date for issuance of the FEIS or EA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing of an EA or issuance of a Notice of Schedule notifies Federal and State agencies of the timing for completion of all necessary reviews and triggers the subsequent need to complete all Federal authorizations within 90 days of the date of issuance of the Commission staff’s FEIS or EA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment Content Guidance (Specificity and Docket Reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person wishing to comment may do so; comments may include statements of support or objections to the project as a whole or to specific aspects of the project. The more specific your comments, the more useful they will be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting comments, reference the applicable docket number (e.g., CP25-299-000) and include specific issues, facts, or evidence to support positions. Use the Commission’s eComment/eFiling systems or mail/paper procedures as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of Service Requirement for Filings
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of all filings in reference to an application must be accompanied by proof of service on all persons listed in the service list prepared by the Commission in the proceeding, in accordance with 18 CFR 385.2010.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure service to all parties on the official service list; failure to properly serve parties may affect acceptance or consideration of filings. Follow the Commission’s service methods and maintain proof of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Interest Determination Standard for Non-FTA LNG Exports
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Natural Gas Act, for an application to export domestically produced natural gas (including LNG) to non-FTA countries, DOE must grant the application unless it finds that the proposed exportation will not be consistent with the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE uses studies (e.g., the 2024 LNG Export Study) and public comments to inform its public interest determinations, considering economic, environmental/climate, energy security, and international considerations. DOE may respond to comments but need not revise the underlying study; both the study and comments inform determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and Method-Specific Submission Instructions (ED Campus-Based Programs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must meet established deadline dates for submission of applications, reports, waiver requests, and other documents to ensure consideration for funding or waiver. Certain items must be submitted electronically through COD (https://cod.ed.gov); others require an original-signed mailed signature page to the FISAP Administrator or submission of scanned supporting documents by email where instructed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific deadlines are listed for each item (e.g., FISAP due October 1, 2025; Perkins Cash on Hand Update due October 31, 2025; waiver requests due various 2026 dates). Electronic submissions must be completed/accepted by 11:59 p.m. ET on the deadline date. Paper documents sent via USPS must be postmarked by the applicable deadline date. Notes explain that the Department will provide additional details in Electronic Announcements posted at least 30 days before the deadline.
